children: CTO Denis Angell highlighted positive progress coinciding with a surge in amendment activity after a scorecard feature launch.
On September 3, Angell disclosed a new feature from the
: a live scorecard for every amendment before it reaches mainnet.

Angell explained the rationale behind the board: Every new XRPL feature ships as an amendment with validators voting it in, and once it's active, it's part of the protocol for good. He added that this deserves real evidence that the feature has been exercised end-to-end on devnet, not just tested in isolation.

The dashboard reads each amendment's full spec surface straight from the node, so nothing is hand-maintained: every transaction type, optional field, flag, result code, ledger entry, and lifecycle. Then it watches devnet and scores each one if it has a validated transaction that has ever touched it. Green cells link to the first transaction that did it. Red cells are the to-do list.
Quantum physics says a system behaves differently once it's observed. Turns out ledgers do too.

48 hours after this board went live: 278 pieces of amendment surface exercised for the first time. Two amendments went from single digits to 100% coverage. Sponsor lit 77 new cells.… https://t.co/c1eG853Sxj
Angell noted that 16 amendments on devnet were being scored correctly, and a daily analysis reads the traffic and writes up what the numbers alone don't show.

Now 48 hours after the board went live, amendment activity has surged, with 278 pieces of amendment surface exercised for the first time. Two amendments went from single digits to 100% coverage. Sponsor lit 77 new cells, and Devnet as a whole is at 91%. Likewise, 8 of the 16 amendments have every cell green, each linked to at least one validated transaction.

Citing a line from quantum physics which says a system behaves differently once it's observed, Angell added, "Turns out ledgers do too," highlighting the importance of observation for system behaviour.

This week, the revamped XRPL website went live with a new design offering clearer paths for institutions, developers, community members, and newcomers to learn about the XRP ecosystem. Developers can find resources and explore use cases across payments, tokenization, and trading.

In separate news, De Vinci Blockchain is hosting a curated Builder Task Force hackathon on the XRP Ledger in Paris from September 11 to 13. Teams will spend the weekend building on the Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), shipping a prototype plus structured feedback on the tooling and docs. The event is capped at 40–50 builders and $10,000 in rewards.

title: XRP Ledger CTO Calls Attention to Amendment Uptick as XRPL Unveils New Tool
